A figure's size on its report's page

Source: R/fig_page_size.R
tfl_fig_page_size.Rd

How big a figure report's figure is drawn and placed: the report sheet's figure_width_in / figure_height_in, each a number of inches (that size), fit (the page's body) or blank (the figure's own size, as rtfreporter places an image: native). The body is the page (the page sheet's width_in / height_in, else its paper_size in its orientation) less its margins; its height less, too, the report's title and footnote lines (and a line between each and the figure), at the page's font size. A report program draws the figure at this size (its text the size its theme says) and the report places it so; the dpi only sets how many pixels it has.

Usage

tfl_fig_page_size(spec, output_id = NULL, native = c(6.5, 4.5))

Arguments

spec

A report definition (tfl_read_report_spec()), or the path(s) to read it from.

output_id

The report, when spec defines several.

native

The figure's own size in inches, c(width, height): what a blank gives (a study's figure style says it by the figure's kind; rtfreporter draws a plot at 6.5 x 4.5).

Value

A list: width_in, height_in (inches, two decimals) and mode (c(width = , height = ): "native", "fit" or "fixed").

Examples

sp <- tfl_table_spec(
  report = data.frame(output_id = "F-1", type = "figure",
                      figure_width_in = "fit"),
  page = data.frame(output_id = NA, paper_size = "letter",
                    orientation = "landscape"),
  titles = data.frame(output_id = "F-1", line = c("1", "2"),
                      center = c("Figure 14.2.1", "Kaplan-Meier")))
tfl_fig_page_size(sp, "F-1")
#> $width_in
#> [1] 9.5
#> 
#> $height_in
#> [1] 4.5
#> 
#> $mode
#>    width   height 
#>    "fit" "native" 
#>
